1	# Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715
     5	
     6	## The Model Substitution Problem
     7	
     8	Commercial LLM API providers charge users for access to specific models (e.g., Llama-3-70B, Qwen2-72B), but the black-box nature of APIs means users have no guarantee the advertised model is actually being served. Providers face strong economic incentives to covertly substitute cheaper alternatives — quantized versions, smaller models, or entirely different architectures — to reduce GPU costs while maintaining pricing.
     9	
    10	The paper formalizes this as a hypothesis testing problem: given samples from the API, can an auditor distinguish the specified model's distribution P_spec(y|x) from an alternative P_actual(y|x)? Substitution types include: (1) smaller models (e.g., 8B instead of 70B), (2) quantized variants (FP8/INT8 instead of FP16), (3) fine-tuned or updated versions, and (4) entirely different model families.
    11	
    12	## Quantization Substitution: Benchmark Impact Is Minimal
    13	
    14	The authors evaluated five model families comparing original precision against FP8 quantization across four benchmarks. The small performance differences make detection extremely challenging.
    15	
    16	| Model | MMLU | GSM8K | MATH | GPQA Diamond |
    17	|---|---|---|---|---|
    18	| Llama-3-8B-Instruct | 62.69 ± 0.18 | 61.14 ± 3.47 | 20.65 ± 3.43 | 22.62 ± 0.22 |
    19	| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 | 62.43 ± 0.26 | 60.90 ± 4.10 | 14.91 ± 2.49 | 20.14 ± 0.24 |
    20	| Llama-3-70B-Instruct | 78.05 ± 0.08 | 88.06 ± 1.44 | 35.69 ± 1.33 | 29.60 ± 0.51 |
    21	| Llama-3-70B-Instruct-FP8 | 77.88 ± 0.13 | 87.35 ± 1.24 | 35.75 ± 1.16 | 33.12 ± 0.30 |
    22	| Gemma-2-9b-it | 71.86 ± 0.08 | 81.80 ± 1.35 | 33.41 ± 0.28 | 28.64 ± 2.97 |
    23	| Gemma-2-9b-it-FP8 | 71.92 ± 0.11 | 79.41 ± 1.14 | 32.53 ± 0.34 | 27.81 ± 3.22 |
    24	| Qwen2-72B-Instruct | 82.18 ± 0.08 | 86.72 ± 1.00 | 37.39 ± 1.41 | 29.93 ± 2.71 |
    25	| Qwen2-72B-Instruct-FP8 | 81.98 ± 0.08 | 86.82 ± 0.97 | 37.67 ± 1.39 | 31.08 ± 1.96 |
    26	| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | 59.15 ± 0.10 | 35.90 ± 4.54 | 8.94 ± 1.24 | 21.60 ± 0.17 |
    27	| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-FP8 | 58.77 ± 0.13 | 32.20 ± 4.02 | 7.68 ± 1.23 | 22.72 ± 0.19 |
    28	
    29	For most models, FP8 scores fall within the error bars of the original, especially on MMLU and GSM8K. Temperature scaling experiments (temperatures 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0) show that higher temperatures degrade all models' performance, further obscuring the substitution signal.
    30	
    31	![Benchmark accuracy vs temperature for five models across four tasks](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    32	
    33	## Log Probability Fingerprinting Defeated by Nondeterminism
    34	
    35	A promising detection approach compares token-level log probabilities between a local reference model and the API. However, the authors demonstrate that production inference environments introduce significant nondeterminism. The same Llama-3-8B model produces different log probabilities depending on the software framework (transformers 4.40 vs 4.50, vLLM 0.6.2 vs 0.8.2) and GPU hardware (A100 vs H100).
    36	
    37	![Log probability variation across inference frameworks and hardware for Llama-3-8B](./assets/figure_5.jpg)
    38	
    39	This inherent variation means an auditor cannot distinguish between a legitimate model served on different infrastructure and an actual substitution, rendering log-probability fingerprinting unreliable in practice.
    40	
    41	## Adversarial Countermeasures
    42	
    43	Beyond passive detection challenges, providers can actively evade audits through: (1) **Randomized substitution** — routing only a fraction p of queries to the cheaper model, making the mixed distribution approach the specified model's distribution as p decreases; (2) **Benchmark evasion** — detecting known benchmark prompts and routing them to the genuine model while serving substitutes for regular traffic. These adversarial strategies make software-only detection fundamentally query-prohibitive.
    44	
    45	## TEEs as the Solution
    46	
    47	The paper proposes Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) — hardware-secured enclaves that provide cryptographic attestation of the code and data being executed. With TEEs (e.g., NVIDIA confidential computing on H100 GPUs), the provider can prove that specific model weights are loaded and that the correct inference code is running, with only modest performance overhead. Unlike ZKPs which are computationally prohibitive for large models, TEEs are practical and deployable today.
    48	
    49	## Key Findings
    50	
    51	- FP8 quantization reduces costs significantly while barely affecting benchmark scores, making it an attractive but nearly undetectable substitution.
    52	- Statistical tests on text outputs (e.g., MMD) require impractically large query budgets and fail against subtle or randomized substitutions.
    53	- Log-probability fingerprinting is defeated by production-level inference nondeterminism across software versions and GPU hardware.
    54	- Adversarial countermeasures (randomized routing, benchmark evasion) further undermine all software-only detection approaches.
    55	- Trusted Execution Environments provide provable, efficient, and robust model integrity guarantees, representing the most actionable solution available today.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# Create 16:9 presentation
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette
DARK_BG = RgbColor(0x1A, 0x1A, 0x1A)
ACCENT = RgbColor(0x00, 0xB4, 0xD6)
WHITE = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC)
MEDIUM_GRAY = RgbColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)
TABLE_HEADER_BG = RgbColor(0x2A, 0x2A, 0x2A)
TABLE_ROW_BG = RgbColor(0x22, 0x22, 0x22)
TABLE_ALT_BG = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x1E, 0x1E)
RED_ACCENT = RgbColor(0xE6, 0x4A, 0x4A)
GREEN_ACCENT = RgbColor(0x4A, 0xE6, 0x4A)

def add_background(slide, color=DARK_BG):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18, bold=False, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(left), Inches(top), Inches(width), Inches(height))
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox

def add_multiline_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, lines, font_size=16, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=1.2):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(left), Inches(top), Inches(width), Inches(height))
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = line
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.alignment = align
        p.space_after = Pt(font_size * (line_spacing - 1))
    return txBox

def add_line(slide, left, top, width, color=ACCENT, thickness=Pt(2)):
    line = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(left), Inches(top), Inches(width), Pt(2))
    line.fill.solid()
    line.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    line.line.fill.background()
    return line

# ============================================
# SLIDE 1: Title Slide
# ============================================
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide1)

add_textbox(slide1, 0.8, 2.2, 11.7, 1.2,
            "Auditing Model Substitution in LLM APIs:",
            font_size=40, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide1, 0.8, 3.3, 11.7, 0.8,
            "Why Software Tests Fail and Hardware Attestation Wins",
            font_size=32, bold=True, color=ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_line(slide1, 0.8, 4.3, 2.5, color=ACCENT, thickness=Pt(3))
add_textbox(slide1, 0.8, 4.6, 11.7, 0.6,
            "Are you getting what you pay for? The trust gap in commercial LLM APIs and the case for verifiable inference.",
            font_size=18, color=LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_textbox(slide1, 0.8, 6.5, 11.7, 0.4,
            "Based on arxiv.org/abs/2504.04715",
            font_size=14, color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ============================================
# SLIDE 2: The Model Substitution Problem
# ============================================
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide2)

add_textbox(slide2, 0.6, 0.4, 12, 0.7,
            "The Model Substitution Problem: Economic Incentives Drive Covert Swaps",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_line(slide2, 0.6, 1.05, 1.8, color=ACCENT, thickness=Pt(2))

add_textbox(slide2, 0.6, 1.3, 12, 1.0,
            "Commercial LLM API providers charge for access to specific models, but the black-box nature of APIs means users have no guarantee the advertised model is actually being served. Providers face strong economic incentives to covertly substitute cheaper alternatives to reduce GPU costs while maintaining pricing.",
            font_size=17, color=LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Four substitution types as boxes
box_data = [
    ("Smaller Model", "8B parameters served\ninstead of 70B"),
    ("Quantized Variant", "FP8/INT8 instead\nof FP16"),
    ("Fine-tuned / Updated", "Different checkpoint\nor revision"),
    ("Different Family", "Entirely different\narchitecture"),
]
box_w = 2.6
box_h = 1.4
start_x = 0.6
start_y = 2.6
gap = 0.35

for i, (title, body) in enumerate(box_data):
    x = start_x + i * (box_w + gap)
    shape = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(x), Inches(start_y), Inches(box_w), Inches(box_h))
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = TABLE_HEADER_BG
    shape.line.color.rgb = ACCENT
    shape.line.width = Pt(1.5)
    tf = shape.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title
    p.font.size = Pt(15)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
    p2.text = body
    p2.font.size = Pt(13)
    p2.font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
    p2.font.name = "Calibri"
    p2.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    p2.space_before = Pt(6)

# Hypothesis testing framework
add_textbox(slide2, 0.6, 4.4, 12, 0.5,
            "Formal Hypothesis Testing Framework",
            font_size=20, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

hypo_box = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.9), Inches(12), Inches(1.8))
hypo_box.fill.solid()
hypo_box.fill.fore_color.rgb = TABLE_ALT_BG
hypo_box.line.color.rgb = MEDIUM_GRAY
hypo_box.line.width = Pt(1)

tf = hypo_box.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "H₀ (Null):    The API returns samples from the specified model distribution P_spec(y|x)"
p.font.size = Pt(17)
p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
p.font.name = "Calibri"
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT

p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
p2.text = "H₁ (Alternative): The API returns samples from a substituted distribution P_actual(y|x)"
p2.font.size = Pt(17)
p2.font.color.rgb = RED_ACCENT
p2.font.name = "Calibri"
p2.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
p2.space_before = Pt(10)

p3 = tf.add_paragraph()
p3.text = "Given only black-box query access, can an auditor reliably reject H₀?"
p3.font.size = Pt(15)
p3.font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
p3.font.name = "Calibri"
p3.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
p3.space_before = Pt(10)

# ============================================
# SLIDE 3: Quantization Benchmark Drop
# ============================================
slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide3)

add_textbox(slide3, 0.5, 0.35, 12.3, 0.7,
            "FP8 Quantization Preserves Most Accuracy — Making Substitution Hard to Detect",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_line(slide3, 0.5, 1.0, 1.8, color=ACCENT, thickness=Pt(2))

add_textbox(slide3, 0.5, 1.15, 12.3, 0.5,
            "Original vs. FP8-quantized scores across four benchmarks for five model families. Drops are often within error bars.",
            font_size=15, color=LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Table
rows, cols = 11, 5
table = slide3.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.7), Inches(12.3), Inches(5.3)).table

col_widths = [3.6, 2.2, 2.2, 2.2, 2.1]
for i, w in enumerate(col_widths):
    table.columns[i].width = Inches(w)

headers = ["Model", "MMLU", "GSM8K", "MATH", "GPQA Diamond"]
table_data = [
    ["Llama-3-8B-Instruct", "62.69 ± 0.18", "61.14 ± 3.47", "20.65 ± 3.43", "22.62 ± 0.22"],
    ["Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8", "62.43 ± 0.26", "60.90 ± 4.10", "14.91 ± 2.49", "20.14 ± 0.24"],
    ["Llama-3-70B-Instruct", "78.05 ± 0.08", "88.06 ± 1.44", "35.69 ± 1.33", "29.60 ± 0.51"],
    ["Llama-3-70B-Instruct-FP8", "77.88 ± 0.13", "87.35 ± 1.24", "35.75 ± 1.16", "33.12 ± 0.30"],
    ["Gemma-2-9b-it", "71.86 ± 0.08", "81.80 ± 1.35", "33.41 ± 0.28", "28.64 ± 2.97"],
    ["Gemma-2-9b-it-FP8", "71.92 ± 0.11", "79.41 ± 1.14", "32.53 ± 0.34", "27.81 ± 3.22"],
    ["Qwen2-72B-Instruct", "82.18 ± 0.08", "86.72 ± 1.00", "37.39 ± 1.41", "29.93 ± 2.71"],
    ["Qwen2-72B-Instruct-FP8", "81.98 ± 0.08", "86.82 ± 0.97", "37.67 ± 1.39", "31.08 ± 1.96"],
    ["Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3", "59.15 ± 0.10", "35.90 ± 4.54", "8.94 ± 1.24", "21.60 ± 0.17"],
    ["Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-FP8", "58.77 ± 0.13", "32.20 ± 4.02", "7.68 ± 1.23", "22.72 ± 0.19"],
]

for c in range(cols):
    cell = table.cell(0, c)
    cell.text = headers[c]
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = TABLE_HEADER_BG
    p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
    p.font.size = Pt(14)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

for r in range(1, rows):
    for c in range(cols):
        cell = table.cell(r, c)
        cell.text = table_data[r-1][c]
        bg = TABLE_ROW_BG if r % 2 == 1 else TABLE_ALT_BG
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = bg
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.font.size = Pt(12)
        p.font.color.rgb = WHITE if c == 0 else LIGHT_GRAY
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER if c > 0 else PP_ALIGN.LEFT
        # Highlight FP8 rows
        if "FP8" in table_data[r-1][0]:
            p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT

# ============================================
# SLIDE 4: Temperature Scaling Degradation
# ============================================
slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide4)

add_textbox(slide4, 0.5, 0.35, 12.3, 0.7,
            "Higher Temperature Amplifies Performance Gaps but Increases Noise",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_line(slide4, 0.5, 1.0, 1.8, color=ACCENT, thickness=Pt(2))

add_textbox(slide4, 0.5, 1.15, 12.3, 0.5,
            "Benchmark accuracy vs. temperature (0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0) for five models across four tasks. At T=2.0, degradation is universal and the substitution signal is obscured by noise.",
            font_size=15, color=LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Insert figure_1.jpg
img_path = "/app/benchmark/assets/figure_1.jpg"
if os.path.exists(img_path):
    slide4.shapes.add_picture(img_path, Inches(1.0), Inches(1.8), width=Inches(11.3))

add_textbox(slide4, 0.5, 6.6, 12.3, 0.5,
            "Figure: Benchmark accuracy vs. temperature for five models across MMLU, GSM8K, MATH, and GPQA Diamond.",
            font_size=12, color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ============================================
# SLIDE 5: Log Probability Nondeterminism
# ============================================
slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide5)

add_textbox(slide5, 0.5, 0.35, 12.3, 0.7,
            "Log Probability Fingerprinting Fails Due to Inference Nondeterminism",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_line(slide5, 0.5, 1.0, 1.8, color=ACCENT, thickness=Pt(2))

add_textbox(slide5, 0.5, 1.15, 12.3, 0.5,
            "The same Llama-3-8B model produces different token-level log probabilities depending on software framework and GPU hardware.",
            font_size=15, color=LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

img_path5 = "/app/benchmark/assets/figure_5.jpg"
if os.path.exists(img_path5):
    slide5.shapes.add_picture(img_path5, Inches(1.0), Inches(1.8), width=Inches(11.3))

add_textbox(slide5, 0.5, 6.6, 12.3, 0.5,
            "Figure: Log-probability variation across inference frameworks (transformers 4.40 vs 4.50, vLLM 0.6.2 vs 0.8.2) and hardware (A100 vs H100).",
            font_size=12, color=MEDIUM_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ============================================
# SLIDE 6: Randomized Substitution
# ============================================
slide6 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide6)

add_textbox(slide6, 0.5, 0.35, 12.3, 0.7,
